optionalrel.title: Optional Relationship
optionalrel.remarks: Defines feasibility of the dependency. When YES (feasible), it is mandatory (HARD constraint). When NO (non-feasible), it is optional (SOFT constraint) and optimizer can choose to respect or not.

useleadlagasshift.title: Use Lead Lag As Shift Hours
useleadlagasshift.remarks: If true, lead lag is understood as shift hours, otherwise (default) it is calendar hours. If shift ends at 6 and task ends at 5 and lead/lag=2h, next task can start next day at shift start (eg 8am) if calendar hours, should start after 9am if shift hours.

predrefwonum.title: Predecessor WONUM
predrefwonum.remarks: Identifies the wonum of the predecessor work order task

optimize.title: Enforce Lead/Lag
optimize.remarks: Allows the relationship to be relaxed by optimization.

maxleadlaghours.title: Maximum Lead Lag Hours
maxleadlaghours.remarks: Maximum lead lag hours to limit max delay between predecessor and successor. Task B must be done within max time X after the end/start of Task A.

reltype.title: Relationship
reltype.remarks: The dependency between work records which determines scheduling order.  This includes Finish to Start, Finish to Finish, Start to Start, and Start to Finish.

leadlaghours.title: Lead/Lag Hours
leadlaghours.remarks: The overlap of, or delay between, work records that have a dependency.  Enter a positive duration for a Lag (delay).  Enter a negative duration for a Lead (overlap).
